The Enlightenment belief in Progress is a powerful, directional view of history toward a better human future.
Christian eschatology provided the foundational Western idea of directional history.
Francis Bacon championed empirical inquiry and 'useful knowledge' as the engine of human progress.
Immanuel Kant defined the Enlightenment as humanity's emergence from self-imposed immaturity.
Hegel viewed world history as the progress of the consciousness of freedom.
Marx posited that history progresses through stages defined by the mode of production.
Nietzsche's 'Last Man' represents a society devoted only to comfort, safety, and shallow happiness.
Cybernetics, founded by Norbert Wiener, studies control and communication in animals and machines.
Deleuze and Guattari's 'Anti-Oedipus' introduced the concept of deterritorialization as a fundamental logic of capitalism.
